welcome_lead: Volcanoes have shaped history. Travel back to Pompeii, sit in a grounded aeroplane, then meet Hawaii's lava!

concepts.def: Italian volcano that destroyed Pompeii in 79 CE.

walkthroughs.body_html: In 79 CE, Vesuvius erupted, burying Pompeii and Herculaneum under ash. The towns were preserved beneath metres of debris, giving us amazing snapshots of Roman life.
In April 2010, this Icelandic volcano sent a huge ash cloud over Europe. Over 100,000 flights were cancelled — ash damages jet engines!
Kilauea is one of the world's most active volcanoes. Its runny lava regularly flows into the sea. In 2018, eruptions destroyed many homes but few people died.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between primary and secondary effects of an earthquake?
options: Primary effects happen first and secondary effects happen the next day.
Primary effects occur immediately as a direct result of shaking (building collapse, deaths); secondary effects follow afterwards (fires, tsunamis, disease, homelessness).
Primary effects are the worst effects and secondary effects are minor.
Because the government forces them to move to cities.

mcqs.q: Why has the Richter scale been largely replaced by the moment magnitude scale?
options: Richter saturates above magnitude ~7 and was calibrated for local Californian quakes; moment magnitude (Mw) measures the total energy released and works for all sizes globally.
The Richter scale is still the standard scale used by all seismologists.
Moment magnitude measures damage while Richter measures shaking.
Because the government forces them to move to cities.
